## Gravity work inside the vertical implicit operator (`implicit-scheme`) {#sec-ch06-vic}

<!-- PROVENANCE

Local symbols: $\mathbf e_m$ is the unit row vector of the normal-momentum unknown; $[\mathsf X]_\rho$ and
$[\mathsf X]_E$ are the mass and energy rows of a block $\mathsf X$. Tracked in ISSUES.md.

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Puts the gravity work into the vertical implicit correction (VIC) so the solve sees the same
energy the explicit stage books: the cell work with `gravity-work: cell`, the face work with `face`, and after
the solve the work of the mass that was projected or clamped. **Switch.** `implicit-scheme` $\neq0$ with
`const-gravity`. **Order.** A linearisation about the stage state. **Defining equation.** @eq-ch06-vic-rows.
:::

The VIC solves each $x_1$ column implicitly for the stage's changes of mass, normal momentum and energy (the
time-integration chapter covers the solve). Gravity enters it twice. The momentum row's mass column and the
energy row's momentum column hold the gravity source Jacobian $\boldsymbol\Phi$, the linearisation of the body force
$\rho g_1$ and of the cell work $\rho v_1g_1$. With `gravity-work: face` the energy row is changed so that it
books the face form of the mass the solve itself moves; booked after the solve instead, that work made a tall
column blow up at acoustic Courant about 66 (chengcli/snapy#283). With `gravity-work: cell` the energy row adds
only the dissipative part of the face form. After the solve two corrections book the work of the mass that the
solve's projection and its availability clamp moved differently from what the matrix assumed, so the booked
energy matches the mass actually moved.

Under `face-wallc` the face work stays outside the operator and is swapped in after the solve, with the wall cells
keeping the cell work; setup warns about it. With the corrected-PE switch on, the energy row also carries part of
that scheme's work (@sec-ch06-dwork). Aliases: chengcli/snapy#283 (face work in the operator), #285 (the
projection and clamp work).

### Derivation

The face form @eq-ch06-dwork-face can be written with the weights
$\omega^{\mathrm{lo}}_i = \tfrac12A_{i-1/2}(x_{1,i}-x_{1,i-1/2})/V_i$ and
$\omega^{\mathrm{hi}}_i = \tfrac12A_{i+1/2}(x_{1,i+1/2}-x_{1,i})/V_i$ as
$W^{\mathrm{face}}_i = 2g_1(\omega^{\mathrm{hi}}_iF_{i+1/2}+\omega^{\mathrm{lo}}_iF_{i-1/2})$. The solve's own
mass flux, linearised, is $F_{i+1/2} = \tfrac12(m_i+m_{i+1}) - \tfrac12[\mathsf A^+]_\rho(\mathbf q_{i+1}-\mathbf q_i)$
with $\mathbf q$ the unknowns and $m=\mathbf e_m\mathbf q$. Substituting, and moving the work to the left-hand
side, the gravity entries of the energy row of block row $i$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}
[\mathsf B_i]_E &= -g_1\,\omega^{\mathrm{lo}}_i\big(\mathbf e_m + [\mathsf A^-]_\rho\big),\\
[\mathsf A_i]_E &= -g_1\big(\omega^{\mathrm{lo}}_i+\omega^{\mathrm{hi}}_i\big)\mathbf e_m
  - g_1\big(\omega^{\mathrm{hi}}_i[\mathsf A^+]_\rho - \omega^{\mathrm{lo}}_i[\mathsf A^-]_\rho\big),\\
[\mathsf C_i]_E &= -g_1\,\omega^{\mathrm{hi}}_i\big(\mathbf e_m - [\mathsf A^+]_\rho\big).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch06-vic-rows}

@eq-ch06-vic-rows is assembled in `vic_assemble_full_impl` from `Phi` and the rows under `face_work`
([`vic_assemble_full_impl.h:101-120`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h#L101-L120)),
with the weights `work_lo` and `work_hi`
([`implicit_hydro.cpp:239-242`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp#L239-L242)).
`vicwork_check.py` `[C1]` ports the rows and finds them equal to minus the linearised face work to
$7\times10^{-15}$ over 200 random rows. On a Cartesian column both weights are $\tfrac14$, and the code's Cartesian
branch writes that value in exactly (`[C2]`). With `gravity-work: cell` the momentum entry stays $-g_1$ from
$\boldsymbol\Phi$, the cell work, and only the $[\mathsf A^\pm]_\rho$ terms are added (`[C3]`).

After the solve the code books $\phi_i$ times the difference between the raw solved mass change, the explicit
change and the mass the projection moved, and the potential-energy flux of the mass the availability clamp moved
minus what was requested. The first vanishes when the solve is applied as solved; the second keeps
$E+\mathrm{PE}_d$ over a closed column (`[C4]`). Checks: `src/snapy_report/ch06/vicwork_check.py`, output
`vicwork_check.out` [sha: the formulas of snapy@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0, ported line for line;
deck: the check itself; run: `python3 vicwork_check.py`, numpy, double].

### Numerical method

@fig-ch06-vic-rows shows the energy-row entries per mode. The rows are assembled once per stage per column, for the
full VIC (`vic_assemble_full`) and the partial VIC (`vic_assemble_partial`) alike, at the stage state, so they
are a linearisation; the step taken is $\Delta t_c$. With `face` the explicit face correction is added to the
right-hand side before the solve, so the energy the solve inverts is the face-form energy, under `face_work_in_operator`
([`hydro_forward.cpp:962-967`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L962-L967)).
The column closure at the ends is the VIC's own, reflecting whatever the $x_1$ boundary; immersed solids get no
projection or clamp work. Wall cells use the same rows with the closure applied.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch06-vic-rows
#| fig-cap: "Gravity entries of the energy row of block row i of the VIC, per gravity-work mode: in the blocks of cell i-1 (B), cell i (A) and cell i+1 (C), m is the normal-momentum column and A-, A+ the mass rows of the Roe dissipation matrices at faces i-1/2 and i+1/2; lo and hi are the face-work weights. With cell the momentum entry is the cell work -g; with face it is the face-weighted average of the three cells."
#| fig-alt: "A two-by-three grid of boxes with formulas: rows gravity-work cell and gravity-work face, columns b[i], a[i], c[i]."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch06.fig_vic_rows import make_fig
make_fig()
```

: Code map of the gravity work in the implicit operator. {#tbl-ch06-vic-code}

1. Form the face weights as `work_lo` and `work_hi` ([`implicit_hydro.cpp:239-242`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp#L239-L242)).
2. Choose the mode flags from `face_work_in_operator` and `gravity_work` ([`implicit_hydro.cpp:270-277`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp#L270-L277)).
3. In `vic_assemble_full_impl`, add the Cartesian or general rows under `face_work` ([`vic_assemble_full_impl.h:101-120`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h#L101-L120)).
4. Add the explicit face correction before the solve, as `gravity_energy_correction` ([`hydro_forward.cpp:962-967`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L962-L967)).
5. After the solve, add `projection_work` and `clamp_work` ([`implicit_hydro.cpp:402-413`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp#L402-L413)).
6. For `face-wallc`, swap in the face work after the solve as `swap` ([`implicit_hydro.cpp:436-443`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp#L436-L443)).

`test_implicit_face_work_operator` puts the column of chengcli/snapy#283 into discrete balance and runs it with
`gravity-work: face`, full and partial VIC, at acoustic Courant 65.6, 197 and 657, requiring `W_TOL` and `EPE_TOL`
([`test_implicit_face_work_operator.py:40-41`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_implicit_face_work_operator.py#L40-L41)). The plain arms run with
`SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT=0`; the `_radial_exact_python` entries run the same scripts with it on and measure
$E+P$. `implicit_gravity_work_holds_under_rk3_stage_weighting` also has a CUDA case. Measured values at the pin are
**missing evidence**.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
`face-wallc` with an implicit scheme books the face work after the solve; a tall column at acoustic Courant about
66 blows up that way (chengcli/snapy#283).
:::

- The rows are a linearisation about the stage state.
- The VIC closes each column as a reflecting wall whatever the $x_1$ boundary (time-integration chapter).
- Combinations with the study switches: @sec-ch12-matrix.
